conversation_digest.summary: Episode thesis: Northeastern's Center for Research Innovation says fiscal year 2026 was a record commercialization year, including nine newly launched companies. The episode should stay with named, sourced examples rather than a campus victory lap. The concrete recent spinouts are InLoop, which says a clinic can 3D-print a custom orthotic in about a day, and Tantu Therapeutics, which is advancing microbe-based therapies for inflammatory bowel disease. Tadavo, Fourier Thermal Solutions, Ada IQ, Pathfind, CellOS, Rheopoint, and ViralNPQ are supporting examples, not equal claims. Founder marketing numbers stay attributed to the founder.

source_messages.text: I have a new topic. It needs to be something related to recent Northeastern University spinouts. Use web search to develop it, then put it through the media platform so I get engaging video content.

story_intent.central_question: What actually left Northeastern's labs in the latest spinout wave, and which of those companies is close enough to a human body to matter on camera?
story_intent.provisional_thesis: CRI's own FY2026 tally is nine new companies and another $25.7 million raised by spinouts, on top of 122 companies and more than $515 million across fifteen years.
story_intent.mens_health_bridge: Men delay foot pain and gut symptoms until the workaround is the injury.
must_keep_lines: Launching is not the same verb as lasting.
Nine companies is a pace. Sixty-one still active is a survival number.
A custom footbed, printed where the patient already is.
